questions.question: A page built once in advance and sent as the same file to every visitor is called a _____ page.
questions.explanation: It is made before anyone visits, so the server only has to hand out a ready file.

questions.question: Which kind of page is built by the server at the moment each visitor asks for it?
questions.explanation: Server-rendered pages are made fresh for each request. C is tempting, but client-rendered pages are built in the browser, not on the server.

questions.question: Why does a static page usually load faster than a server-rendered one?
questions.answer: It is already built, so nothing has to be computed, and a CDN keeps copies near each visitor, so the file travels a short distance.
questions.explanation: No work at request time plus a nearby copy means the visitor gets the file almost immediately.

questions.question: Is it true that a CDN is a single big server that all visitors connect to?
questions.explanation: A CDN is many servers spread around the world, each with a copy of the files, so visitors use a nearby one.

questions.question: Making a website work in several languages is called internationalisation, shortened to _____.
questions.explanation: There are 18 letters between the "i" and the "n" of "internationalisation".

questions.question: Why is it useful to give each language its own URL, such as /en and /fr?
questions.answer: Each version can be shared, bookmarked and indexed by search engines, and each can be a ready-made static page.
questions.explanation: With one address per language, the address itself says which language you get, for people and for search engines.

questions.question: Is it true that automatic language detection means the site no longer needs a language switch?
questions.explanation: Detection is only a guess from browser settings. Users still need a visible way to pick another language.

questions.question: Is it true that in Accept-Language, a language written without a q-value counts as the top preference?
questions.explanation: A missing q-value means q=1, the highest score.

questions.question: A browser sends "fr, en;q=0.9, de;q=0.5" to a site with only English and German. Which language should it get?
questions.explanation: French scores highest but the site doesn't have it, so the next best supported language wins: English (0.9) beats German (0.5).

questions.question: Why does a multilingual site save the visitor's language choice in a cookie?
questions.answer: The browser sends the cookie back on every visit, so the site remembers the choice next time, even if the browser's languages say something else.
questions.explanation: A cookie is a note the browser keeps and returns with each request, so the site can read the earlier choice.

questions.question: What does the lang attribute on the <html> tag tell?
options: Which programming language the server uses
The language the page's text is written in
questions.explanation: It labels the page's language for screen readers, translators and search engines. C is tempting, but that is the job of hreflang links.

questions.question: Links that tell search engines "this page also exists in another language, here" use the attribute _____.
questions.explanation: Each link gives a language code and the address of that version, so search results show the right one.
